name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API to send, read, update, and delete messages, and to list channels, users, and threads. Use when Gemini CLI needs to post messages to Slack, read channel history or thread replies, resolve channel names, add reactions, or otherwise work with Slack through its REST API.

# Slack API

Work with Slack through the Web API at `https://slack.com/api/`.

## Authentication

- Require a bot or user token (`xoxb-...` or `xoxp-...`) from the user via an environment variable or secure input. Never hardcode, guess, or fabricate credentials.
- Send the token as the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header on every request.
- Before calling a method, verify the token's scopes cover the method's requirements (e.g., `chat:write` for `chat.postMessage`, `channels:history` for reading public channel history).
- If the API returns `"error": "missing_scope"` or `"not_authed"`, stop and tell the user which scope the token is missing.

## Request pattern

- Endpoint: `https://slack.com/api/<method>`
- Use POST with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` for JSON payloads (the exact charset parameter is required by Slack for some methods) or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` for form data.
- Every response is an envelope: `{"ok": true, ...}` or `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}`. Always check `ok` before trusting payload fields; surface `error` to the user.
- Prefer immutable Slack IDs (`C...` channels, `U...` users, `D...` DMs, `ts` timestamps) over display names; resolve names only when needed.

## Common workflows

### Post a message
1. Resolve the target channel: call `conversations.list` and match the channel `name`; keep its `id`.
2. Call `chat.postMessage` with `channel`, `text`, and optionally `blocks`, `thread_ts` (to reply in a thread), and `mrkdwn`.
3. Check `ok`. On success, keep the returned `ts` and `channel` for later updates or replies.

### Read messages
- `conversations.history` lists messages in a channel: pass `channel`, `limit` (1–999, default 100), `cursor` for pagination, and `oldest`/`latest` (Unix timestamps) to bound the window.
- `conversations.replies` fetches a thread: pass `channel` and the parent `ts`.

### Update and delete
- `chat.update` with `channel`, `ts`, and the new `text` or `blocks`.
- `chat.delete` with `channel` and `ts`.

### Workspace data
- `users.list` / `users.info` for users.
- `conversations.list` for channels (pass `types=public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim` to include DMs).
- `reactions.add` with `channel`, `name` (emoji without colons), and `timestamp`.

## Pagination

- List-style methods return `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Loop, passing `cursor`, until it is `""` or absent.
- Keep `limit` reasonable (e.g., 100–200) to avoid oversized payloads.

## Rate limits

- Slack rate-limits per method by tier (Tier 1 ≈ 1 req/s, Tier 2 ≈ 20 req/s, Tier 3 ≈ 50 req/s, Tier 4 ≈ 100 req/s). Most chat methods are high-tier, but never assume: on HTTP 429, read the `Retry-After` header and wait that many seconds before retrying; back off exponentially on repeated 429s or 5xx.

## Message formatting

- Use mrkdwn: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, fenced code blocks, `>quote`.
- Link format: `<https://example.com|Display text>`; bare URL: `<https://example.com>`.
- Emoji shortcodes: `:tada:`.
- Escape `&`, `<`, `>` in user-supplied text to prevent unintended formatting.
- For structured messages, use Block Kit (`blocks`): `section`, `divider`, `context`, `actions` with `button` elements.

## References

- `references/methods.md` — payload examples and response shapes for common methods.
- `references/formatting.md` — mrkdwn and Block Kit examples.
```

# Common Slack API Methods

## Table of contents

- chat.postMessage
- chat.update / chat.delete
- conversations.list
- conversations.history
- conversations.replies
- users.list / users.info
- reactions.add
- api.test

## chat.postMessage

Sends a message to a channel or thread.

Required scope: `chat:write`

Request (JSON):

```json
{
  "channel": "C1234567890",
  "text": "Hello from an automated workflow",
  "mrkdwn": true
}
```

Reply in a thread by adding `"thread_ts": "1712345678.000100"`.

Success response:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "channel": "C1234567890",
  "ts": "1712345678.000100",
  "message": {}
}
```

Keep `ts` and `channel` to update or delete the message later.

## chat.update

Updates an existing message.

Required scope: `chat:write`

Request (JSON):

```json
{
  "channel": "C1234567890",
  "ts": "1712345678.000100",
  "text": "Updated text"
}
```

## chat.delete

Deletes a message.

Required scope: `chat:write`

Request (JSON):

```json
{
  "channel": "C1234567890",
  "ts": "1712345678.000100"
}
```

## conversations.list

Lists channels and conversations the bot can see.

Required scopes: `channels:read` (plus `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read` for private channels and DMs).

Query params: `types=public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim`, `limit`, `cursor`.

Response:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "channels": [
    { "id": "C1234567890", "name": "general" }
  ],
  "response_metadata": { "next_cursor": "" }
}
```

## conversations.history

Reads recent messages in a channel.

Required scopes: `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, or `mpim:history` depending on conversation type.

Query params: `channel`, `limit`, `cursor`, `oldest`, `latest` (Unix timestamps).

Response:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "messages": [
    { "type": "message", "user": "U1234567890", "text": "...", "ts": "1712345678.000100" }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "response_metadata": { "next_cursor": "..." }
}
```

## conversations.replies

Fetches all messages in a thread.

Required scopes: same as history.

Query params: `channel`, `ts` (parent message timestamp).

## users.list / users.info

- `users.list`: all users visible to the token (scope `users:read`). Paginated via `cursor`.
- `users.info`: one user by `user` ID (scope `users:read`).

## reactions.add

Adds an emoji reaction.

Required scope: `reactions:write`

Request (JSON):

```json
{
  "channel": "C1234567890",
  "name": "tada",
  "timestamp": "1712345678.000100"
}
```

## api.test

Checks connectivity and token validity without side effects.

GET or POST `https://slack.com/api/api.test` — returns `{"ok": true}` when the API is reachable (works without a token too).
